newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The Inkatha Freedom Party decided to testify before the "truth commission" because the murder of thousands of its supporters was being ignored, party leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi said.
- A rates boycott in Sandton near Johannesburg is gaining momentum, as officials conceded there had been a massive decline in revenue from businesses and residents.

- The South African Chamber of Business business confidence index recovered almost half a point in August after the announcement of measures to curb crime and an apparent stabilisation of the economy.
- Mercedes-Benz (South Africa) broke ranks with the six major motor vehicle manufacturers on Thursday by signing a plant-level agreement providing for a pay rise linked to inflation.
- Church schools have accused Gauteng province of undermining religious freedom by cutting their subsidies by 30 percent.
BUSINESS REPORT
- State transport company Transnet has brought in a retired judge to try to settle a growing controversy over the alleged misuse of a company credit card by an official, Transnet's chairman said.
- Anglo American Corp is expected to show a huge capital profit, or surplus, on the sale of its 20 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp (Johnnic)
- Columbus Stainless Steel, the world's largest integrated producer of stainless steel, has drawn up a plan to win back domestic customers who complained of erratic quality.
- Anglo American Corp is considering developing two new deep gold mines at record depths and will spend 33 million rand on a seismic survey covering 60 sq km south of the Western Deep Levels mine.
- Zenith Concessions, whose diamond exploration activities on the west coast have come to nought, is to acquire a gem-polishing and cutting business.
THE STAR
- The government has sounded a strong warning to Sandton residents, businesses and property owners about the implications of a rates boycott launched after a 200 percent increase in rates.
- The government is planning to take advantage of the high service fees South African banks charge their customers, by slapping on a further 14 percent value added tax from October 1.

- An anonymous donor who agreed to pay out 10 million rand to rescue the Sarafina II AIDS-awareness play is a white South African businessman who does not want to be identified, the Public Protector said.
- President Nelson Mandela and Graca Machel are to discuss getting married, Archbishop Desmond Tutu said.
